issue.title: Run a 24 h full-load crash test on win2 after its BIOS update

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** After Nathan's BIOS update of win2 (BIOS 3.40, microcode 0x121, newer ME): a 24 h full-load crash test on the new firmware, with the same records as #177. Recommended by win2 in #177's summary.
- **The load.** All of win2's cores, on Python 3.14 (venv-t177, after #179's setup there). It mixes #177's amplitude copies with the scipy RK path that preceded negative-mass's stacked crashes; ask the negative-mass coordinator for a runnable call of it. It also includes `hp` work from #179's identity checks.
- **The records.** `crash_watch.py` (every crash of any process, with time, module, offset and code), Core Temp readings within a minute of each crash, the 5-minute `sensor_log.txt` (temperatures, clocks, package power, utilization, free memory), and the WHEA, Kernel-Power 41 and BugCheck events.
- **The firmware.** Record the BIOS, microcode and ME versions after the update, as #177 did before it.

**Why.** win2 crashed eight times on the old firmware (BIOS 1.38, microcode 0x110), in python312.dll, libflint and numpy at random offsets (#82, #177). #177's loop on Python 3.14 did not test the upgrade: zero crashes in 4.47 h has a 44% chance at the old rate. This test asks whether the new firmware stops the crashes under a load that includes the paths that crashed.

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- Every amplitude copy hashes to fd6b5ef2…. A different hash names the first differing σ string.
- The crash count over 24 h is set against the old rate of about one per 5.5 h under load. Zero crashes in 24 h has about a 1% chance at that rate.
- Each crash's temperature is set against the baseline's median and maximum under the same load.
- The firmware versions are recorded.

**Depends on.** The BIOS update, #179 on win2.
